name: Swampscott
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Swampscott, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Swampscott, MA: Breakfast with Santa, gingerbread house decorating, an Elf Workshop, the Festival of Trees and the holiday parade.
lede: Swampscott does Christmas as a small seaside town: the Recreation Department fills the Clarke School and the Town Hall lawn with holiday programs, and the Police Association sends Santa through the neighborhoods in its annual parade.
celebrates: Most of Swampscott's Christmas runs through the Recreation Department. It hosts a Festival of Trees at the Clarke School, where decorated trees and wreaths stay on display for a week before they are raffled off, plus gingerbread house sessions, a gingerbread decorating contest and a home decorating contest. Breakfast with Santa, shared with Toys for Local Children, raises money for local kids. The Holiday Festival on the Town Hall lawn brings vendors, the town tree lighting and a visit from Mrs. Claus, and the Swampscott Police Association holiday parade rolls past with fire trucks, floats and Santa. The First Church in Swampscott opens the season with its long running Let It Snow Fair.
lastyear: In 2025 the First Church in Swampscott held its 177th Let It Snow Fair on November 22 at 40 Monument Avenue. The first Swampscott Festival of Trees filled the Clarke School with nearly 30 decorated trees and wreaths, and about 100 groups came on the first night. On Saturday, December 13, the Police Association parade carried cruisers, fire trucks, ambulances and Santa along Essex, Burrill, Paradise, Vinnin, Salem and Humphrey Streets, while the Town Hall lawn festival offered kiddie fire truck rides and Mrs. Claus with her donkey reindeer.
facts: The First Church in Swampscott Congregational has held its Let It Snow Fair for 178 years, according to the Swampscott Tides, with members selling handmade goods, books and baked goods to fund the church. The town newsletter counts the Recreation Department's gingerbread house contest as a 16 year tradition, while the Festival of Trees only began in 2025. In 2025 the town decorated with a Christmas tree built from lobster crates, and one gingerbread entry at the festival was a copy of it. The donkeys that visit with Mrs. Claus come from Minis with a Mission, a nonprofit.
trains: Swampscott has its own MBTA Commuter Rail stop. Swampscott station sits at Burrill Street and Railroad Avenue on the Newburyport/Rockport Line, with trains to North Station in Boston and a mini high level platform for level boarding. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs its Holiday Express through Christmas lights. In Lowell, the National Streetcar Museum has hands-on streetcar exhibits for kids, and the Boston and Maine Railroad Historical Society displays steam locomotive No. 410 on Dutton Street.

faq: Swampscott's Recreation Department runs most of the season: the Festival of Trees at the Clarke School, gingerbread sessions and a gingerbread contest, Breakfast with Santa with Toys for Local Children and a Holiday Festival on the Town Hall lawn with the tree lighting. The Swampscott Police Association adds its annual holiday parade with fire trucks, floats and Santa riding through town.
Where does the Swampscott holiday parade go?

The Police Association parade starts at Swampscott High School and travels Essex Street to Burrill Street, then Paradise Road, Vinnin Street, Salem Street and Humphrey Street, and the festivities continue at Town Hall. In 2025 the Swampscott Tides reported cruisers, fire trucks, ambulances, floats and Santa himself. Families watch from the sidewalks along the route, so pick a spot close to home.
What is the Swampscott Festival of Trees?

It is a Recreation Department fundraiser at the Clarke School. Families, businesses and groups decorate a tree or wreath with a theme of their choice, the displays stay up for about a week and then each one is raffled off. The first festival in 2025 had nearly 30 trees and wreaths, from a police department tree to a nursery school handprint wreath.
Who runs Breakfast with Santa in Swampscott?

The Swampscott Recreation Department and Toys for Local Children (TLC) co-sponsor it at the Senior Center on Essex Street. All proceeds support TLC, which collects gifts for local children, and families are asked to bring a new, unwrapped toy if they can. The Rec Department warns every year that the breakfast sells out, so register early.
Can kids meet Mrs. Claus in Swampscott?

Yes. At the 2025 Holiday Festival on the Town Hall lawn, Mrs. Claus listened to children's Christmas wishes alongside her donkey reindeer from Minis with a Mission, a nonprofit that also offered bags of glittery reindeer feed for a donation. The festival also had kiddie fire truck rides, food and dessert vendors, artisan tables and the town tree lighting.
